title.value: Two types of human TCR differentially regulate reactivity to self and non-self antigens
title.justification: The title reflects the core research focus of the paper, which is the understanding of how different types of TCR (T-cell Receptors) interact with self and non-self antigens.
title.quote: Two types of human TCR differentially regulate reactivity to self and non-self antigens

extractions.description: Based on analyses of TCR sequences from over 1,000 individuals, the paper investigates two types of TCRs in humans: neonatal and TDT-dependent. It explores the production, diversity, and role of these TCRs in relation to factors like thymic output and activity of terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TDT). It is discovered that neonatal TCRs are prevalent from birth, while TDT-dependent ones emerge later, impacting conditions like graft-versus-host disease, immune response diversification, and effects of aging and sex on TCR diversity.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The research focus is on immunological science, particularly the diversity and function of T-cell receptors. While it has potential implications for human health, it doesn't centrally address climate or ecological sustainability.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Based on analyses of TCR sequences from over 1,000 individuals, we report that the TCR repertoire is composed of two ontogenically and functionally distinct types of TCRs.

primary_category.justification: The paper is focused on immunological research rather than topics directly related to climate or ecological sustainable development.
primary_category.quote: Based on analyses of TCR sequences from over 1,000 individuals, we report that the TCR repertoire is composed of two ontogenically and functionally distinct types of TCRs.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no secondary themes related to sustainable development as the paper is centered on immunology.
secondary_categories.quote: Factors decreasing thymic output (age, male sex) negatively impact TCR diversity.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no specific alignment with climate or ecological sustainable development sub-categories as the paper does not address these areas.
primary_sub_category.quote: Based on analyses of TCR sequences from over 1,000 individuals, we report that the TCR repertoire is composed of two ontogenically and functionally distinct types of TCRs.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper does not address areas directly linked to sustainable development sub-categories.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Neonatal TCRs derived from TDT-negative progenitors persist throughout life, are highly shared among subjects, and are reported as disease-associated.

applications.value: Analysis of TCR diversity and its impact on diseases like graft-versus-host disease
applications.justification: The paper discusses how TCR diversity influences disease outcomes, such as graft-versus-host disease, indicating its application in understanding immune responses.
applications.quote: Acute graft-vs-host disease correlates with a high proportion of TDT-dependent TCRs.

new_primary_category.justification: The study is not relevant to any of the existing climate or ecological sustainable development categories.
new_primary_category.quote: The TCR repertoire is composed of two layers: neonatal and TDT-dependent layer

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No new sub-category is required as the paper's focus is outside climate or ecological sustainability themes.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: A salient finding was the identification of two non-redundant CDR3 repertoire layers based on physical characteristics, including length, number of insertions, and V/J gene usage.
